claim: Ciliates span a much larger range of speeds than flagellates, up to 7 mm/s.
source: Ciliates span a much larger range of speeds, up to 7 mm/s, whereas generally smaller flagellates remain in the sub-mm/s range.
evidence: The manuscript directly states the speed ranges observed in the data.

claim: Flagellates generally remain in the sub-mm/s speed range.
source: Ciliates span a much larger range of speeds, up to 7 mm/s, whereas generally smaller flagellates remain in the sub-mm/s range.
evidence: The manuscript directly states the speed ranges observed in the data.

claim: The average cell size differs fourfold between flagellates and ciliates (31 µm for flagellates and 132 µm for ciliates).
source: The average cell size differs fourfold between the populations (31 µm for flagellates and 132 µm for ciliates) and the distributions, plotted in Figure 2—figure supplement 2, are biased towards the low-size end but they are quantitatively different.
evidence: The manuscript provides specific measurements of average cell sizes from collected data.

claim: Log-normal distributions are widely observed across nature in areas such as ecology, physiology, geology and climate science.
source: Log-normal distributions are widely observed across nature in areas such as ecology, physiology, geology and climate science, serving as an empirical model for complex processes shaping a system with many potentially interacting elements (Limpert et al., 2001), particularly when the underlying processes involve proportionate fluctuations or multiplicative noise (Koch, 1966).
evidence: The manuscript cites literature to support this general statement about log-normal distributions.

claim: Log-normal distributions serve as an empirical model for complex processes with many potentially interacting elements.
source: Log-normal distributions are widely observed across nature in areas such as ecology, physiology, geology and climate science, serving as an empirical model for complex processes shaping a system with many potentially interacting elements (Limpert et al., 2001), particularly when the underlying processes involve proportionate fluctuations or multiplicative noise (Koch, 1966).
evidence: The manuscript cites literature to support this characterization of log-normal distributions.

claim: Log-normal distributions particularly emerge when underlying processes involve proportionate fluctuations or multiplicative noise.
source: Log-normal distributions are widely observed across nature in areas such as ecology, physiology, geology and climate science, serving as an empirical model for complex processes shaping a system with many potentially interacting elements (Limpert et al., 2001), particularly when the underlying processes involve proportionate fluctuations or multiplicative noise (Koch, 1966).
evidence: The manuscript cites literature to support this mechanism for log-normal distributions.

claim: The published literature includes a sufficiently large amount of unbiased data to see the whole distribution.
source: Since the data are accurately described by this distribution, we conclude that the published literature includes a sufficiently large amount of unbiased data to be able to see the whole distribution.
evidence: The manuscript infers this from the quality of fit to the log-normal distribution.

claim: The integrated absolute difference between the flagellate and ciliate distributions is 0.028.
source: Furthermore, both the integrated absolute difference between the distributions (0.028) and the Kullback-Leibler divergence (0.0016) are very small (see Materials and methods), demonstrating the close similarity of the two distributions.
evidence: The manuscript provides this calculated metric to quantify distribution similarity.

claim: The Kullback-Leibler divergence between the flagellate and ciliate distributions is 0.0016.
source: Furthermore, both the integrated absolute difference between the distributions (0.028) and the Kullback-Leibler divergence (0.0016) are very small (see Materials and methods), demonstrating the close similarity of the two distributions.
evidence: The manuscript provides this calculated metric to quantify distribution similarity.

claim: Data for ciliates were sourced from 26 research articles.
source: Data for ciliates were sourced from 26 research articles, while that for flagellates were extracted from 48 papers (see Appendix 1).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states the number of source articles.

claim: Data for flagellates were extracted from 48 papers.
source: Data for ciliates were sourced from 26 research articles, while that for flagellates were extracted from 48 papers (see Appendix 1).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states the number of source articles.

claim: Swimming speeds reported in various studies have been measured under different physiological and environmental conditions.
source: Notably, swimming speeds reported in the various studies have been measured under different physiological and environmental conditions, including temperature, viscosity, salinity, oxygenation, pH and light.
evidence: The manuscript acknowledges the variability in measurement conditions across the literature.

claim: The data are considered as arising from a random sampling of a wide range of environmental conditions rather than representing a uniform environment.
source: Therefore we consider the data not as representative of a uniform environment, but instead as arising from a random sampling of a wide range of environmental conditions.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this interpretation of the data collection.

claim: Unicellular eukaryotes comprise a vast, diverse group of organisms that covers virtually all environments and habitats.
source: Unicellular eukaryotes comprise a vast, diverse group of organisms that covers virtually all environments and habitats, displaying a menagerie of shapes and forms.
evidence: The manuscript states this as general knowledge about unicellular eukaryotes.

claim: Hundreds of species of the ciliate genus Paramecium are found in marine, brackish, and freshwater reservoirs.
source: Hundreds of species of the ciliate genus Paramecium (Wichterman, 1986) or flagellated Euglena (Buetow, 2011) are found in marine, brackish, and freshwater reservoirs
evidence: The manuscript cites literature to support this statement about Paramecium distribution.

claim: The green algae Chlamydomonas is distributed in soil and fresh water world-wide.
source: the green algae Chlamydomonas is distributed in soil and fresh water world-wide (Harris et al., 2009)
evidence: The manuscript cites literature to support this statement about Chlamydomonas distribution.

claim: Parasites from the genus Giardia colonize intestines of several vertebrates.
source: parasites from the genus Giardia colonize intestines of several vertebrates (Adam, 2001)
evidence: The manuscript cites literature to support this statement about Giardia.

claim: Motility is crucial for nutrient acquisition and avoidance of danger in unicellular eukaryotes.
source: One of the shared features of these organisms is their motility, crucial for nutrient acquisition and avoidance of danger (Bray, 2001).
evidence: The manuscript cites literature to support this functional role of motility.

claim: Single-celled organisms have developed in a variety of directions in the process of evolution, resulting in a large spectrum of swimming modes.
source: In the process of evolution, single-celled organisms have developed in a variety of directions, and thus their rich morphology results in a large spectrum of swimming modes (Cappuccinelli, 1980).
evidence: The manuscript cites literature to support this evolutionary perspective.

claim: Many swimming eukaryotes actuate tail-like appendages called flagella or cilia to generate thrust.
source: Many swimming eukaryotes actuate tail-like appendages called flagella or cilia in order to generate the required thrust (Sleigh, 1975).
evidence: The manuscript cites literature to support this description of propulsion mechanisms.

claim: Thrust is achieved by actively generating deformations along the flagellum, giving rise to a complex waveform.
source: This is achieved by actively generating deformations along the flagellum, giving rise to a complex waveform.
evidence: The manuscript describes this mechanism based on established knowledge.

claim: The flagellar axoneme is a bundle of nine pairs of microtubule doublets surrounding two central microtubules, termed the '9 + 2' structure.
source: The flagellar axoneme itself is a bundle of nine pairs of microtubule doublets surrounding two central microtubules, termed the '9 + 2' structure (Nicastro et al., 2005), and cross-linking dynein motors, powered by ATP hydrolysis, perform mechanical work by promoting the relative sliding of filaments, resulting in bending deformations.
evidence: The manuscript cites literature to support this structural description.

claim: Cross-linking dynein motors, powered by ATP hydrolysis, perform mechanical work by promoting the relative sliding of filaments, resulting in bending deformations.
source: The flagellar axoneme itself is a bundle of nine pairs of microtubule doublets surrounding two central microtubules, termed the '9 + 2' structure (Nicastro et al., 2005), and cross-linking dynein motors, powered by ATP hydrolysis, perform mechanical work by promoting the relative sliding of filaments, resulting in bending deformations.
evidence: The manuscript cites literature to support this mechanistic description.

claim: Eukaryotic flagella exhibit a diversity of forms and functions.
source: Although eukaryotic flagella exhibit a diversity of forms and functions (Moran et al., 2014), two large families, 'flagellates' and 'ciliates', can be distinguished by the shape and beating pattern of their flagella.
evidence: The manuscript cites literature to support this statement about flagellar diversity.

claim: Two large families, 'flagellates' and 'ciliates', can be distinguished by the shape and beating pattern of their flagella.
source: Although eukaryotic flagella exhibit a diversity of forms and functions (Moran et al., 2014), two large families, 'flagellates' and 'ciliates', can be distinguished by the shape and beating pattern of their flagella.
evidence: The manuscript states this as a basis for the study's classification scheme.

claim: Flagellates typically have a small number of long flagella distributed along the bodies.
source: Flagellates typically have a small number of long flagella distributed along the bodies, and they actuate them to generate thrust.
evidence: The manuscript describes this morphological characteristic based on established knowledge.

claim: The set of observed movement sequences in flagellates includes planar undulatory waves and traveling helical waves.
source: The set of observed movement sequences includes planar undulatory waves and traveling helical waves, either from the base to the tip, or in the opposite direction (Jahn and Votta, 1972; Brennen and Winet, 1977).
evidence: The manuscript cites literature to support this description of flagellar motion patterns.

claim: Propulsion of ciliates derives from the motion of a layer of densely-packed and collectively-moving cilia.
source: In contrast, propulsion of ciliates derives from the motion of a layer of densely-packed and collectively-moving cilia, which are short hair-like flagella covering their bodies.
evidence: The manuscript describes this propulsion mechanism based on established knowledge.

claim: Cilia are short hair-like flagella covering ciliate bodies.
source: In contrast, propulsion of ciliates derives from the motion of a layer of densely-packed and collectively-moving cilia, which are short hair-like flagella covering their bodies.
evidence: The manuscript provides this definition based on established knowledge.

claim: Cilia may be used for transport of the surrounding fluid.
source: Cilia may also be used for transport of the surrounding fluid, and their cooperativity can lead to directed flow generation.
evidence: The manuscript states this as an additional function of cilia based on established knowledge.

claim: Ciliary cooperativity can lead to directed flow generation.
source: Cilia may also be used for transport of the surrounding fluid, and their cooperativity can lead to directed flow generation.
evidence: The manuscript states this as a consequence of ciliary motion based on established knowledge.

claim: In higher organisms, ciliary flow generation can be crucial for internal transport processes, as in cytoplasmic streaming within plant cells.
source: In higher organisms this can be crucial for internal transport processes, as in cytoplasmic streaming within plant cells (Allen and Allen, 1978), or the transport of ova from the ovary to the uterus in female mammals (Lyons et al., 2006).
evidence: The manuscript cites literature to support this example of ciliary function.

claim: Cilia are crucial for the transport of ova from the ovary to the uterus in female mammals.
source: In higher organisms this can be crucial for internal transport processes, as in cytoplasmic streaming within plant cells (Allen and Allen, 1978), or the transport of ova from the ovary to the uterus in female mammals (Lyons et al., 2006).
evidence: The manuscript cites literature to support this example of ciliary function.

claim: Spermatozoa were not included in the study because they lack the capability to reproduce and are thus not living organisms.
source: we do not include spermatozoa since they lack (ironically) the capability to reproduce and are thus not living organisms; their swimming characteristics have been studied by Tam and Hosoi, 2011
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states the rationale for excluding spermatozoa.

claim: The number of flagella in ciliates and flagellates leads to a clear morphological division between the two groups.
source: The inset shows that the number of flagella in both groups leads to a clear division.
evidence: The manuscript states this based on data shown in the figure inset.

claim: The observed log-normal randomness captures a universal way for ecological niches to be populated by abundant microorganisms with similar propulsion characteristics.
source: Our results suggest that the observed log-normal randomness captures a universal way for ecological niches to be populated by abundant microorganisms with similar propulsion characteristics.
evidence: The manuscript proposes this interpretation based on the statistical findings.

claim: The distributions of swimming speeds among species do not necessarily reflect the distributions of swimming speeds among individuals.
source: We note, however, that the distributions of swimming speeds among species do not necessarily reflect the distributions of swimming speeds among individuals, for which we have no available data.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly acknowledges this limitation of the study.

claim: Bin widths in histograms were chosen according to the Freedman-Diaconis rule.
source: Bin widths in histograms in Figure 2 and Figure 3 have been chosen separately for ciliates and flagellated eukaryotes according to the Freedman-Diaconis rule (Freedman and Diaconis, 1981) taking into account the respective sample sizes and the spread of distributions.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly describes the methodology used for data visualization.

claim: The fitting procedures use the raw data via the maximum likelihood estimation method, not the processed histograms.
source: We emphasize that the fitting procedures use the raw data via the maximum likelihood estimation method, and not the processed histograms, hence the estimated parameters are insensitive to the binning procedure.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly describes the fitting methodology.

claim: A sum of independent log-normal random variables can be well approximated by another log-normal random variable.
source: Despite that, there is general agreement that a sum of independent log-normal random variables can be well approximated by another log-normal random variable.
evidence: The manuscript states this as established statistical knowledge.

claim: The sum of identically distributed equally and positively correlated joint log-normal distributions converges to a log-normal distribution of known characteristics.
source: It has been proven by Szyszkowicz and Yanikome (2009) that the sum of identically distributed equally and positively correlated joint log-normal distributions converges to a log-normal distribution of known characteristics but for uncorrelated variables only estimations are available (Beaulieu et al., 1995).
evidence: The manuscript cites literature to support this mathematical result.

claim: The distributions contain enough data to be unbiased and seen in full.
source: We use these results to conclude that our distributions contain enough data to be unbiased and seen in full.
evidence: The manuscript infers this from the statistical properties and cited mathematical results.

claim: The probability distributions of swimming speed for flagellates and ciliates are accurately represented by log-normal distributions.
source: Despite the morphological and size differences between these groups, each of the two probability distributions of swimming speed are accurately represented by log-normal distributions, with good agreement holding even to fourth moments.
evidence: The abstract states this as a main finding based on statistical analysis.

claim: Good agreement with log-normal distributions holds even to fourth moments.
source: Despite the morphological and size differences between these groups, each of the two probability distributions of swimming speed are accurately represented by log-normal distributions, with good agreement holding even to fourth moments.
evidence: The abstract states this as evidence for the quality of the log-normal fit.

claim: Scaling of the distributions by a characteristic speed for each data set leads to a collapse onto an apparently universal distribution.
source: Scaling of the distributions by a characteristic speed for each data set leads to a collapse onto an apparently universal distribution.
evidence: The abstract states this as a main finding of the analysis.

claim: The results suggest a universal way for ecological niches to be populated by abundant microorganisms.
source: These results suggest a universal way for ecological niches to be populated by abundant microorganisms.
evidence: The abstract proposes this interpretation of the findings.

source: Figure 1 shows a tree encompassing the phyla of organisms studied and sketches of a representative organism from each phylum.
evidence: The manuscript describes the content of Figure 1.

claim: A large morphological variation is clearly visible among the studied organisms.
source: A large morphological variation is clearly visible.
evidence: The manuscript states this observation based on Figure 1.

claim: Both aquatic and parasitic groups include ciliates and flagellates.
source: Both groups include ciliates and flagellates.
evidence: The manuscript states this based on the phylogenetic tree in Figure 1.
